questions.stem: Which vitamin deficiency leads to night blindness (nyctalopia) and eventually to complete blindness if uncorrected?
questions.explanation: Vitamin A (retinol) is essential for synthesis of rhodopsin, the light-sensitive pigment in rod cells of the retina. Its deficiency first causes night blindness and, if prolonged, progresses to xerophthalmia (dry eye), corneal damage, and total blindness.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: Scurvy, characterized by bleeding gums, slow wound healing, and fragile blood vessels, is caused by deficiency of:
questions.explanation: Vitamin C (ascorbic acid) is essential for collagen synthesis. Its deficiency leads to scurvy — characterized by haemorrhages, spongy/bleeding gums, poor wound healing, and joint pain. British naval physician James Lind demonstrated that citrus fruits cured scurvy in 1747.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: Goitre (enlargement of the thyroid gland) is caused by deficiency of which mineral?
questions.explanation: Iodine is essential for the synthesis of thyroid hormones (thyroxine T4 and triiodothyronine T3). Its deficiency causes the thyroid gland to enlarge (goitre) as it works harder to trap more iodine. In children, iodine deficiency causes cretinism (stunted growth and intellectual disability).
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: Rickets in children (characterized by soft, deformed bones) and osteomalacia in adults are caused by deficiency of:
questions.explanation: Vitamin D is essential for calcium absorption in the intestines and calcium deposition in bones. Its deficiency causes rickets in children (soft, bowed legs, delayed tooth eruption) and osteomalacia in adults (soft bones, pain). Sunlight (UV-B) enables its synthesis in skin.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: Essential amino acids are defined as those that:
options: Cannot be synthesized by the body and must be obtained through diet
Are found exclusively in animal-based protein sources
Are required only during illness or recovery
Can be synthesized from other amino acids if dietary intake is low
questions.explanation: Of the 20 amino acids needed for protein synthesis, 9 are 'essential' (histidine, isoleucine, leucine, lysine, methionine, phenylalanine, threonine, tryptophan, valine) — the body cannot synthesize them and must get them from food. Non-essential amino acids can be synthesized internally.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: Beriberi, affecting the nervous system (dry beriberi) and cardiovascular system (wet beriberi), is caused by deficiency of:
questions.explanation: Thiamine (Vitamin B1) is essential as a coenzyme in carbohydrate metabolism (pyruvate dehydrogenase complex). Its deficiency causes beriberi: dry beriberi (peripheral neuropathy, muscle weakness) and wet beriberi (heart failure, oedema). It was historically common in populations eating polished rice.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: Pellagra, characterized by the '4Ds' (Dermatitis, Diarrhoea, Dementia, and if untreated, Death), is caused by deficiency of:
questions.explanation: Niacin (Vitamin B3), as a precursor to NAD and NADP, is essential for energy metabolism. Its deficiency causes pellagra — sun-sensitive dermatitis on exposed skin, gastrointestinal symptoms, and neurological manifestations. Pellagra was historically common in populations dependent on corn (maize) without niacin supplementation.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: The fat-soluble vitamins, which are absorbed with dietary fats and stored in the liver and adipose tissue, are:
options: B complex vitamins and Vitamin C
Vitamins A, D, E, and K
questions.explanation: Vitamins A, D, E, and K are fat-soluble — they require dietary fat for absorption, are stored in body fat and liver, and excess can cause toxicity. Vitamins B-complex and C are water-soluble — excess is excreted in urine and they must be consumed regularly.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: Pernicious anaemia (megaloblastic anaemia where red blood cells are abnormally large and few) is caused by deficiency of:
questions.explanation: Vitamin B12 (cyanocobalamin) is essential for DNA synthesis and red blood cell maturation. Its deficiency causes megaloblastic (pernicious) anaemia and neurological damage. B12 is found only in animal products; vegans and strict vegetarians must supplement. Intrinsic factor (from stomach) is needed for its absorption.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: Which mineral is a key constituent of haemoglobin (the oxygen-carrying protein in red blood cells)?
questions.explanation: Iron is the central component of haem in haemoglobin and myoglobin. Each haemoglobin molecule has 4 haem groups, each containing one iron atom that binds oxygen. Iron deficiency causes iron-deficiency anaemia (microcytic, hypochromic) — the most common nutritional deficiency worldwide.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: Vitamin K (phylloquinone) plays a critical role in:
options: Immune cell activation and T-cell production
Blood coagulation (synthesis of clotting factors II, VII, IX, X)
Protection of the retina from UV damage
questions.explanation: Vitamin K is essential for the synthesis of several clotting factors (prothrombin/Factor II, and Factors VII, IX, X) in the liver. Its deficiency leads to bleeding disorders. Newborns are given a Vitamin K injection to prevent haemorrhagic disease of the newborn.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: Fluorosis caused by excess fluoride intake primarily damages which tissues?
questions.explanation: Dental fluorosis causes mottling/white/brown staining and pitting of tooth enamel. Skeletal fluorosis causes bone and joint pain, stiffness, and eventually deformity. Fluoride-contaminated groundwater is a major issue in states like Rajasthan, Gujarat, Andhra Pradesh, and Telangana.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: Deficiency of which B vitamin during early pregnancy is strongly associated with neural tube defects (NTDs) like spina bifida and anencephaly in the developing foetus?
questions.explanation: Folic acid (Vitamin B9) is essential for DNA synthesis and cell division during the early weeks of pregnancy. Deficiency during the periconceptional period (weeks 3-4 of gestation, when the neural tube closes) causes NTDs. Women planning pregnancy are advised to take folic acid supplements.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: Kwashiorkor, a severe form of malnutrition in children, is primarily caused by:
options: Severe deficiency of dietary protein with relatively adequate caloric intake
Excess fat intake causing metabolic syndrome
Vitamin A deficiency causing immune suppression
questions.explanation: Kwashiorkor is protein-energy malnutrition with a predominantly protein deficiency. Characteristic features: oedema (swollen belly due to low albumin), skin lesions, hair discolouration, fatty liver, and irritability. It typically occurs when a child is weaned onto a low-protein, high-starch diet. Marasmus, in contrast, is total caloric starvation.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: Among the three macronutrients, which provides the highest caloric density per gram?
questions.explanation: Fats (lipids) provide 9 kcal per gram — more than double the energy of carbohydrates and proteins (both 4 kcal/g). This is because fats are more reduced (more C-H bonds). Alcohol provides 7 kcal/g. Dietary fibre provides ~2 kcal/g (partially fermented by gut bacteria).
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: Vitamin D synthesis in the human body is triggered by:
options: Dietary calcium intake stimulating parathyroid hormone
Exposure of skin to sunlight (UV-B radiation, 290-315 nm)
Consumption of green leafy vegetables rich in precursor compounds
questions.explanation: 7-dehydrocholesterol in skin is converted to cholecalciferol (Vitamin D3) by UV-B radiation (290-315 nm). This is then hydroxylated in the liver (25-OH-D3) and kidney (1,25-OH2-D3 = calcitriol, the active form). Dark-skinned people in low-sunlight regions are at higher risk of Vitamin D deficiency.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: Marasmus, another severe form of protein-energy malnutrition, is caused by:
options: Protein deficiency with adequate caloric intake
Severe deficiency of both total calories (energy) and protein
questions.explanation: Marasmus is total starvation — severe deficiency of both calories and protein. Children with marasmus appear 'wasted' (extreme loss of fat and muscle), with a 'wizened old man' appearance, sunken eyes, and visible ribs. Unlike kwashiorkor, oedema is absent. It typically occurs in infants before age 1.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: Vitamin A deficiency, beyond causing night blindness, can lead to which severe eye condition involving dryness and damage of the cornea?
options: Xerophthalmia (Bitot's spots, corneal ulceration, and blindness)
Colour blindness (congenital defect in cone cells)
questions.explanation: Chronic Vitamin A deficiency causes xerophthalmia — progressing from night blindness → conjunctival xerosis → Bitot's spots (foamy white patches) → corneal xerosis → keratomalacia (corneal softening/ulceration) → irreversible blindness. Vitamin A supplementation prevents hundreds of thousands of preventable blindness cases annually.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: Which mineral is most critical for the formation and maintenance of bones and teeth, and also plays essential roles in muscle contraction, nerve impulse transmission, and blood clotting?
questions.explanation: Calcium (99% stored in bones and teeth as hydroxyapatite) is the most abundant mineral in the human body. The remaining 1% in blood and soft tissues is critical for muscle contraction, neurotransmitter release, blood clotting (activates clotting factors), and enzyme function. Deficiency causes osteoporosis in adults.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: Vitamin E (tocopherol) primarily functions in the body as:
options: An activator of clotting factor synthesis
A promoter of long bone growth in children
An antioxidant that protects cell membranes from oxidative damage by free radicals
A catalyst for energy release from glucose in mitochondria
questions.explanation: Vitamin E (alpha-tocopherol is the most active form) is a powerful fat-soluble antioxidant that protects polyunsaturated fatty acids in cell membranes and lipoproteins from oxidation by free radicals. It also plays a role in immune function and skin health.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: The energy value of 1 gram of carbohydrate (or protein) is approximately:
questions.explanation: Both carbohydrates and proteins yield approximately 4 kcal (17 kJ) per gram when fully oxidized. Fat yields 9 kcal/g; alcohol 7 kcal/g. This is based on the Atwater energy conversion factors used in nutritional labelling worldwide.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: Biotin (Vitamin B7) deficiency, which causes hair loss, skin rash, and neurological symptoms, is commonly triggered in people who regularly eat large amounts of:
options: Raw egg whites (which contain avidin, a protein that binds and blocks biotin absorption)
questions.explanation: Raw egg whites contain avidin, a glycoprotein that tightly binds biotin and prevents its intestinal absorption. Cooking denatures avidin, eliminating this effect. Biotin deficiency is also seen in prolonged parenteral nutrition and heavy alcohol use.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: Zinc is an essential trace mineral involved in which of the following functions?
options: Wound healing, immune function, DNA synthesis, and enzyme activity (in >300 enzymes)
Oxygen transport in red blood cells
Blood pressure regulation via renin-angiotensin system
Thyroid hormone production and iodine metabolism
questions.explanation: Zinc is a cofactor for over 300 enzymes and is involved in DNA and RNA synthesis, protein synthesis, immune function (T-lymphocyte development), wound healing, taste and smell, and growth. Deficiency causes growth retardation, delayed sexual maturation, skin lesions, and impaired immune response.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: The Recommended Dietary Allowance (RDA) for protein for an average sedentary adult is approximately:
options: 100 g per day (regardless of body weight)
60 g per day (fixed for all adults)
0.8 g per kg body weight per day (~48-60 g/day for a 60-75 kg adult)
questions.explanation: The standard RDA for protein is 0.8 g/kg body weight/day for a sedentary adult. For a 60 kg person, this is 48 g/day. Athletes, pregnant women (add 25 g/day), and lactating women require more. ICMR (Indian Council of Medical Research) recommends ~0.83-1.0 g/kg/day for Indians.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: Water-soluble vitamins (B-complex and Vitamin C), unlike fat-soluble vitamins, are NOT stored significantly in the body. This means that excess amounts are:
options: Stored in the liver and released slowly
Converted to energy in the citric acid cycle
Excreted in the urine — hence they must be consumed daily
Stored in adipose (fat) tissue for up to 6 months
questions.explanation: Water-soluble vitamins (all B vitamins and Vitamin C) are not significantly stored. Excess is rapidly excreted in urine, which means they must be supplied regularly through the diet. This also means overdose toxicity is rare (unlike fat-soluble vitamins A, D, E, K which can accumulate).
questions.subject: Biology
